paragraphs: Growth has downshifted without breaking: real GDP printed 1.5% annualized in the second quarter, down 2.3 points year-over-year and in the 29th percentile of 79 years of history, while industrial production creeps along at 1.08% year-over-year. The labour market is the puzzle. July payrolls fell 23,000, a 43,000 swing from the prior month and the 19th percentile of the postwar record, yet the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%, initial claims sit at 203,000 in the 6th percentile of the past decade, job openings rose to 7.271m in the 81st percentile, and the Sahm rule reads -0.03. That is a low-hiring, low-firing economy rather than a contracting one. The consumer is spending from a position of visible strain: retail sales are up 5.0% year-over-year, but the savings rate has collapsed to 3.0%, the 6th percentile of 67 years, and UMich sentiment at 55.2 is 2.13 standard deviations below normal despite a 5.7-point monthly bounce. Housing is the clearest casualty, with starts down 176,000 in a month to 1.239m and home prices decelerating to 1.5% year-over-year.

Disinflation has stalled well above target. Headline CPI runs 3.304% and PCE 3.701%, both up more than half a point over the year, and core PCE at 3.344% has gone nowhere in a month while core CPI at 2.467% is the one benign number in the set. Markets are not fully convinced this ends well: the 10-year breakeven is 2.31% and the 5y5y forward also 2.31%, the latter in the 85th percentile of ten years. The Fed has nonetheless cut, with effective fed funds at 3.63%, 70bp below a year ago, and the long end has repriced against it — the 10-year at 4.73% sits in the 99th percentile of the past decade, up 51bp year-over-year, and the 30-year at 5.22%. The curve has fully disinverted, with 2s10s at 41bp and 10Y-3M at 84bp, though both flattened modestly over the past month as the front end backed up from 3.78% to 3.84% at one month. A broad dollar down 2.04 points to 118.7 adds a mild inflationary nudge and a tailwind to exporters.

Credit is the loudest vote of confidence in the expansion. High-yield OAS at 2.63% has tightened 22bp in a month and 21bp on the year, leaving it in the 2nd percentile of three years, and investment-grade at 0.80% sits in the 30th percentile despite a 1bp monthly widening. The rating buckets tell a subtler story: BB compressed from 1.73% to 1.52% and single-B from 3.04% to 2.72%, while AAA, AA and A each widened a basis point and CCC widened from 10.34% to 10.42%. Compression in the middle of the stack alongside widening at the distressed tail is the signature of a late-cycle reach for yield, not broad-based health. The Chicago Fed NFCI at -0.566 confirms accommodative financial conditions, M2 grows 5.4% year-over-year, and the Fed's balance sheet is roughly flat at $6.731trn. With VIX at 14.92 and the S&P 8.4% above its 200-day average, the regime model scores 0.725 and calls expansion — but four of its five inputs are market prices, and only the yield curve at 0.5 and industrial relative strength at 0.0 reflect the real economy.
headwinds: Payrolls fell 23,000 in July and GDP growth halved to 1.5% annualized
Core PCE stuck at 3.344% with 5y5y forward inflation at 2.31%, the 85th percentile
The 10-year at 4.73% sits in the 99th percentile of a decade, mortgages at 6.66%
Savings rate at 3.0% and sentiment at 55.2 leave consumers with no cushion
CCC spreads widened to 10.42% even as BB and B compressed sharply
tailwinds: High-yield OAS at 2.63%, the 2nd percentile of three years, keeps refinancing cheap
Claims at 203,000 and unemployment at 4.1% show no firing wave
Fed funds at 3.63%, 70bp lower year-over-year, with 2s10s positive at 41bp
NFCI at -0.566 and M2 growth of 5.4% signal accommodative conditions
VIX at 14.92 and the S&P 8.4% above its 200-day average

sectors.headline: Rates tax the growth premium
sectors.outlook: XLK's 21.6% six-month lead survived a 4.73% ten-year, but the 6.0% three-month give-back prices exactly what a 99th-percentile yield costs.

sectors.headline: Banks bank the curve
sectors.outlook: XLF's 11.2% three-month relative gain tracks a 41bp 2s10s slope and high-yield spreads at 2.63%, the 2nd percentile of three years.

sectors.headline: Defence pays, for once
sectors.outlook: XLV's 14.5% three-month lead answers payrolls at -23,000 and 1.5% GDP; its -3.9% six-month figure shows how recently it was unloved.

sectors.headline: Shoppers spend, savers vanish
sectors.outlook: Retail sales grow 5.0% yearly while savings sink to 3.0% and sentiment to 55.2; XLY trails 2.2% over one month.

sectors.headline: Staples stale, not spoiled
sectors.outlook: XLP's 2.9% three-month edge reversed to -2.8% in one month, an expansion regime scoring 0.725 punishing groceries bought for safety.

sectors.headline: Advertising waits on confidence
sectors.outlook: XLC's -17.2% six-month deficit narrowed to +0.3% in one month as ad budgets ride 5.0% retail sales against a 4.73% discount rate.

sectors.headline: Factories idle, index flat
sectors.outlook: XLI's 0.45% three-month relative strength scored zero in the regime model, matching industrial production growth of 1.08% and a 5.3% monthly slip.

sectors.headline: Crude carries the quarter
sectors.outlook: XLE gained 11.0% relative over three months and 4.7% in one, helped by a broad dollar down 2.04 points to 118.7.

sectors.headline: Metals mend, slowly
sectors.outlook: XLB's 2.5% three-month gain repairs a -12.6% six-month hole as a cheaper dollar meets industrial production growth of just 1.08%.

sectors.headline: Bonds outbid the bond proxy
sectors.outlook: XLU shed 22.0% relative over six months and 7.5% in one, outbid by a 5.22% thirty-year Treasury and a 14.92 VIX.

sectors.headline: Mortgages mug the landlords
sectors.outlook: XLRE fell 4.8% relative in a month as mortgages hit 6.66%, starts dropped 176,000 to 1.239m and home prices rose 1.5%.
